- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for rebound.
- Model overestimates in early forecast horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply 1–2% downward correction for short-term bias.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days of forecast > true, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to align with recent mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.6), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, apply 2–3% upward adjustment for momentum carryover.
